newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu, Arafat discuss further peace steps.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Arafat discuss further peace steps.

text.p: Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu and the Palestinians' Yasser Arafat met at their border on Sunday to discuss expanding self-rule and the operation of Palestinian sea and air ports, officials said.

Chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said Arafat, the Palestinian president, wanted to talk about Israel's withdrawal of troops from West Bank rural areas planned for early March, the ports, and preparations for crucial "final-status" talks.
"We want to agree on preparations to resume final-status talks which should commence in the middle of next month," Erekat told Israel Radio.
The Palestinians also want to operate an airport in the southern Gaza Strip and build a seaport on the Mediterranean.

The summit is a followup to last month's U.S.-brokered Israel-PLO deal that handed 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule and reaffirmed a future three-stage Israeli pullback in the rural West Bank committed to in previous peace deals.

"The commitment is that the first stage of the further redeployment will occur on March 7 and the government of Israel certainly intends to keep that commitment," Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said before the start of the meeting.

Naveh told Army Radio that in line with a letter from then-U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher that accompanied the Hebron deal, Israel alone would determine the scope of the three withdrawals.
The PLO has said the size of the pullbacks, due to end by mid-1998, is a matter for negotiation.

"I hope it will be a meeting in which it will be possible to strengthen the trust between the sides on the basis of the principle of reciprocity in keeping commitments by both sides in the negotiations," Naveh said.
Netanyahu had put off the meeting, initially set for Thursday, after 73 Israeli soldiers died in the collision of two helicopters. It was Israel's worst military air disaster.
Erekat said Arafat would demand Israel stop building Jewish settlements, confiscating land and revoking the residency of East Jerusalem Palestinians living outside the city.
Netanyahu's aide David Bar Bar-Ilan had said that all the "nitty-gritty" issues in the Hebron accord would be discussed as well as Israeli demands that the PLO respect its commitments.
"Prime Minister Netanyahu will obviously bring up the question of reciprocity regarding items included in the 'Note for the Record' which is attached to the Hebron agreement," Bar-Illan said.
The "Note for the Record" reaffirms the commitment by both sides to implement their 1995 interim peace deal and outlines the responsibilities of both the Israelis and Palestinians.
In it the Palestinians pledged to revise the Palestinian National Charter, which calls for the destruction of the state of Israel, and to fight terror.

Israel was due to free 25 Palestinian women prisoners on Monday or Tuesday, officials for both sides said. Palestinian sources said they were the total of women prisoners among the 5,000 Palestinians held by Israel.
Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi said he will not sign a recommendation to release three of the women because one was convicted of murder and the other two were found guilty of attempted murder.

A Justice Ministry spokeswoman said Netanyahyu could sign the recommendations to be sent to President Ezer Weizman. Meanwhile, Israel's High Court issued an order barring the prisoner release until it hears a petition against it on Monday morning, a courts spokesman said.
